rows.purpose: Open an owned mechanical engine and recover the selected full-model session safely.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-PLATFORM require safe startup, but charter section 4 gives 1.0 its own runtime and six layer boundaries. The server-source injection and experiment HTTP installation are replaced while ownership and recovery guarantees survive.
requirements: X-01: Make a clean Windows checkout and installed payload load the immutable model and matching proofs with their declared byte hashes; enforce canonical text bytes rather than relaxing manifest checks.
Validate the complete model identity before exposing state; recover the journal and acquire the session lock before announcing readiness.
Keep platform startup outside the mathematical engine; use EngineProcess for any owned local engine process, including authenticated health, graceful shutdown and parent-pipe recovery.
Replace the 0.4 server-source injection with the selected 1.0 boundary without assuming that its HTTP protocol or process split carries over.
rows.notes: All rows in this file are stage 2.2 proposals from source inventories, not owner sign-off or runtime test evidence. The packet briefing SHA-256 matches a9e8153c1c3de5f4ae1b52b7c5ebd684dbb686aef50ace33bbb97c054cff09ea; flows remain provisional, and no Windows/DirectX, physical-input or performance claim is made.

rows.purpose: Compare complete effects of existing macro revisions explicitly selected by the solver.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-CHECK retain candidate analysis under solving-workflow.md section 7. Its ranking and explanations must fit the shared 1.0 context without choosing a macro or treating a score as permission (command-table.md section 1).
requirements: Analyse only solver-selected existing revisions with identical Prepare and Cleanup inputs, full collateral and the current goal, block and protection context.
Keep comparison detached from the real draft and puzzle state; ranking never selects, inserts or executes a macro.
Bind each result to model identity, exact macro revisions, full-state hash and state/workspace/protection revisions; edits invalidate the comparison.
Explain contributions and unavailable evidence, keeping evidence state, heuristic score, goal progress and execution permission separate.

rows.purpose: Open a safely isolated full-model workspace for practice or an explicitly requested experiment.
rows.reason: F-LEARN and F-PLATFORM retain isolation, while the 2 October 2026 design decision section 7 requires one application entry with a labelled practice copy. G1/G2 browser launch modes and browser-opening switches are replaced by that entry and explicit development tooling.
requirements: X-01: Test startup from clean Windows checkout bytes and an installed payload against immutable asset and proof hashes.
Create or select explicitly scoped isolated data for practice and experiments; never substitute a personal solve or modify it.
Use the same full model and one product entry; identify a practice copy clearly and keep development experiment modes out of normal startup.
Preserve owned-process cleanup, authenticated readiness and graceful shutdown without inheriting browser redirects or separate G1/G2 product doors.

rows.purpose: Explain what the solver's complete operation would achieve and what evidence or protection prevents a conclusion.
rows.reason: F-CHECK uses analysis of the solver's own operation, allowed by solving-workflow.md sections 4.1 and 7. The 1.0 explanation separates permission from progress and evidence from heuristic scores, as required by command-table.md section 1.
requirements: Evaluate the whole Prepare/Macro/Cleanup operation on all labels, including exact block gains, losses, residual changes, protected damage and witness length.
Version and explain any scoring rule; an unknown reference, hard error or protection conflict must not appear as a low numeric score.
A legal protection-preserving operation may remain executable with an unmet goal; preparation need not improve the current score.
Return reasons and evidence for the supplied operation without generating an alternative solving macro or changing the draft.

rows.purpose: Inspect exact piece cycles, orientation changes and sticker correspondences in actual and predicted states.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-ENDGAME require complete effects and residuals (solving-workflow.md sections 3.4 and 4.1). The 2 October 2026 design decision section 6 puts these observations in linked Global and Local views rather than carrying over the 0.4 graph presentation.
requirements: D-03: Consult a revision-bound forecast and inspection cache before rebuilding an After state during paging; verify reuse and invalidation with headless paging measurements.
Distinguish macro-body, Macro-phase and complete-operation scopes; include full collateral even when display or interaction filters hide affected objects.
Identify actual versus conditional occupants, fixed positions, source-to-destination edges and slot frames without relabelling mechanical state.
Keep pagination and view selection detached from the puzzle; expose totals and unavailable reference evidence instead of implying an empty graph means completion.
Supply both linked views from one context and revision; state, role, macro, reference or protection changes invalidate predicted observations.

rows.purpose: Launch a verified native workspace with controlled engine ownership and an isolated development session.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM retains controlled startup and evidence-bound launches, but charter sections 4 and 5 reject inheritance of the retained MPUlt/Managed DirectX runtime. The launch purpose moves to the selected 1.0 application and its explicit experiment harness.
requirements: B-003: Declare only present, tracked harness inputs and prove the development build and launch work from a clean checkout with the approved toolchain.
X-01: Validate canonical checkout and packaged model/proof bytes before engine startup without changing the immutable manifest identity.
Bind launches to accepted build inputs and recheck their hashes before and after the run; a build rejected for changing inputs must never be reused.
Replace retained-runtime copying and G1/G2 product modes with the selected 1.0 host behind narrow platform interfaces.
Use EngineProcess for owned local engine processes and isolate explicit experiments; do not run regression fixtures during normal startup.
Preserve graceful shutdown within the owned-process grace and separate source, fixture, actual Windows/DirectX and performance evidence.

rows.purpose: Observe pieces, buffers and block requirements at explicit boundaries of the solver's draft.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-CHECK need Actual, after-Prepare, after-Macro and after-Cleanup observations in solving-workflow.md section 4. Their detached mathematical semantics remain unchanged when re-hosted.
requirements: Evaluate chronological source-to-destination effects on detached states and show the boundary, base-state hash and complete operation identity.
An intermediate boundary is an observation, not a Net protection pass; label unchecked prefixes explicitly and apply Strict checks only when requested.
Do not project already executed steps again; disclose truncation and unknown references while retaining complete effect and protection analysis.
Keep actual puzzle state and execution permission unchanged by inspection.

rows.purpose: Obtain a reproducible host build whose executable is bound to accepted source, model and tool inputs.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM and charter section 5 E7 retain build traceability. Charter section 4 replaces the C#/.NET Framework/Managed DirectX build recipe with the selected 1.0 toolchain rather than dropping provenance.
requirements: B-003: Every declared source, harness and tool input must resolve from a clean checkout; a missing required input fails before producing an accepted build.
Bind product, model, compiler, build recipe and relevant tool/runtime inputs to the output identity and digest.
Publish an accepted reusable receipt only after all input and output checks pass; rejected or interrupted compilations cannot seed reuse.
A build-only operation must neither open a user session nor start the application, and must remain separate from platform-specific runtime preparation.

rows.purpose: See exact filter matches and counts for objects in actual or projected inspection states.
rows.reason: F-NAVIGATE and F-CHECK retain observational filter evaluation under solving-workflow.md section 4.3. The filter remains separate from the full mechanical analysis and from noninteractive reference display.
requirements: Evaluate each detached actual or projected state against the captured filter context and report piece/sticker totals and per-object matches.
Invalid rules produce unavailable metadata and unknown matches; filters never change labels, legal generators or the scope of collateral and protection checks.
Keep reference visibility, interaction eligibility and mechanical membership separate and invalidate per-reply caches when their inputs change.

rows.purpose: Identify the exact source and build behind a result without compiling or starting a session.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM and charter section 5 E7 require traceable builds and honest evidence. Identity reporting survives with the 1.0 product and tool inventory instead of the retained host's bindings.
requirements: Distinguish source identity from full build identity and list the input roles each binds; an unavailable compiler or runtime leaves the build identity unknown.
Report immutable model and harness input digests without compiling, writing files or opening user data.
Keep diagnostics bounded and sanitized; do not expose credentials, personal paths or raw machine diagnostics in public evidence.

rows.purpose: Inspect the exact finite orientation group and fixed-slot parameters of a named nonbuffer position.
rows.reason: F-ENDGAME retains orientation and reference inspection under solving-workflow.md sections 3.4 and 7. Listing mathematical parameters does not choose or output a solving macro.
requirements: Validate the supplied orbit and nonbuffer position against one certified immutable slot chart and enumerate exact group elements with reference identifiers.
Return parameters as observations only; do not emit a correction recipe, match an element to the current residual or select a macro.
Keep unavailable or stale certificates explicit and never interpret a permitted nonidentity residual as solved.
rows.notes: U6-033 combines parameter inspection with generated endgame recipes; this counterpart link concerns its inspection parts only, while U2-013, U2-015, U2-017 and U2-019 propose deleting recipe generation.

rows.purpose: Run the private frozen Python engine executable through its 0.4 launcher bootstrap.
rows.reason: This entry exists only for the 0.4 frozen source layout and process split, which charter section 4 says 1.0 does not inherit. F-PLATFORM ownership and startup validation survive in U2-001 and U2-014 without requiring this private executable.
rows.notes: Proposed removal is limited to the private frozen-engine bootstrap; authenticated ownership, input identity validation and session recovery are retained by the new startup requirements.

rows.purpose: Obtain a newly constructed placement-star solving recipe for supplied orbit, auxiliary and frame parameters.
rows.reason: EndgameLibrary.compose family=placement-star outputs a new solving recipe, even though its parameters are explicit. That crosses solving-workflow.md section 7 and charter section 5: the solver supplies or chooses their own macro and the program supplies analysis.
rows.notes: This proposal removes generated solving recipes, not inspection of finite orientation parameters, analysis of solver-entered endgames, named-target setup search or explicit composition and reuse of the solver's own macros. U6-033 contains both surviving inspection and prohibited construction purposes.

rows.purpose: Open the installed application on a chosen session and leave it without losing work.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-PLATFORM retain normal application launch under charter sections 4 and 5 E7. The 2 October 2026 design decision section 7 replaces G1/G2 and retained-runtime startup with one entry, direct resume and a practice copy.
requirements: Verify package and model identities before session access and keep application files separate from declared user-data directories.
Preserve existing preferences, journal recovery and the session lock; initialize defaults only for genuinely new data.
Provide one product entry and direct context resume, with a clearly identified full-model practice copy.
Remove Managed DirectX discovery/copying and dependence on the private frozen Python engine; the selected architecture decides the new host boundary.
Use EngineProcess for any owned local engine process and preserve authenticated readiness, graceful shutdown and parent-pipe recovery.
Normal startup must neither compile a host nor run regression fixtures or diagnostics.

rows.purpose: Obtain a newly constructed two-star orientation-transfer solving recipe for supplied position and frame parameters.
rows.reason: EndgameLibrary.compose family=transfer outputs a new solving recipe, even though its parameters are explicit. That crosses solving-workflow.md section 7 and charter section 5: the solver supplies or chooses their own macro and the program supplies analysis.
rows.notes: This proposal removes generated solving recipes, not inspection of finite orientation parameters, analysis of solver-entered endgames, named-target setup search or explicit composition and reuse of the solver's own macros. U6-033 contains both surviving inspection and prohibited construction purposes.

rows.purpose: Understand a startup failure and the available way to recover or retry safely.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-PLATFORM retain failure reporting, while charter section 5 E6 and D2 require actionable errors and designed failure states. The 0.4 message box or generic stderr line is replaced by the new shell and scoped diagnostic results.
requirements: Report what failed, why and a safe next action using typed error categories without exposing credentials or private paths.
Keep failed readiness, recoverable session errors and unknown outcomes distinct; never discard or reset user data to make startup succeed.
Write diagnostic reports only to an explicitly scoped destination, separate from public error wording and normal startup.

rows.purpose: Obtain a newly constructed buffer-A orientation-correction solving recipe for supplied auxiliary and frame parameters.
rows.reason: EndgameLibrary.compose family=buffer-a outputs a new solving recipe, even though its parameters are explicit. That crosses solving-workflow.md section 7 and charter section 5: the solver supplies or chooses their own macro and the program supplies analysis.
rows.notes: This proposal removes generated solving recipes, not inspection of finite orientation parameters, analysis of solver-entered endgames, named-target setup search or explicit composition and reuse of the solver's own macros. U6-033 contains both surviving inspection and prohibited construction purposes.

rows.purpose: Check that an application package contains exactly its declared verified resources before using it.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM and charter section 5 E7 retain package integrity independent of the selected runtime. The resource and architecture contract is rebuilt for 1.0 without inheriting the 0.4 frozen bundle layout.
requirements: Verify supported manifest versions, exact file-set closure and every declared file size and digest; reject missing, altered or unexpected payloads.
Bind checks and reports to the actual package and model identities and preserve upstream attribution and licence notices.
A resource-only check must not open a session, start the engine or renderer, or claim actual Windows/DirectX or final release acceptance.

rows.purpose: Obtain a newly constructed final-buffer commutator solving recipe for supplied auxiliaries and group elements.
rows.reason: EndgameLibrary.compose family=final-b outputs a new solving recipe, even though its parameters are explicit. That crosses solving-workflow.md section 7 and charter section 5: the solver supplies or chooses their own macro and the program supplies analysis.
rows.notes: This proposal removes generated solving recipes, not inspection of finite orientation parameters, analysis of solver-entered endgames, named-target setup search or explicit composition and reuse of the solver's own macros. U6-033 contains both surviving inspection and prohibited construction purposes.

rows.purpose: Verify exact engine transactions and, separately, recovery after the owning launcher dies.
rows.reason: The coarse claude:S2-11 joins two distinct diagnostic purposes split by codex:S2-64 and codex:S2-65. F-PLATFORM needs both, but mathematical transaction evidence and process-death recovery require different acceptance experiments under AGENTS.md.

parts.purpose: Verify the installed engine's full-model analysis, transaction, undo and reopen guarantees on fresh fixture data.
parts.reason: F-PLATFORM supports F-CHECK and F-EXECUTE, and charter sections 2 and 4 require exact mechanics with a new runtime. Rebuild this explicit acceptance fixture at the new boundary and compare it with the differential oracle.
requirements: Run only on fresh isolated fixture data, checking all 259,800 labels, matching invariant/frame evidence, explicit reviewed legal turns, commit, undo and reopen.
Bind results to exact source/build/model identities; do not carry over 0.4 endpoint names or generate a solving macro for the fixture.
Verify durable commit outcomes separately from refresh and graceful shutdown, and never run these fixtures during normal startup.
Report headless fixture evidence separately from actual Windows/DirectX, physical input and performance acceptance.

parts.purpose: Verify that an owned local engine exits recoverably when its launcher disappears.
parts.reason: F-PLATFORM retains parent-pipe recovery under AGENTS.md Persistence and process ownership. The experiment belongs to the selected owned-process boundary rather than forcing the 0.4 frozen process split into 1.0.
requirements: For any owned local engine process, exercise real parent EOF through EngineProcess on fresh isolated data and verify bounded termination and session-lock release.
Reopen after the death and verify the last durable state and journal with recovery intact; an identity or health report alone cannot prove recovery.
Keep the launcher-death experiment an explicit fixture outside normal startup and label its platform and source/build evidence.

rows.notes: claude:S2-11 is intentionally present in both parts because it covers both diagnostics; each fine inventory row is assigned only to its own purpose.

rows.purpose: Inspect all proper ordered local frames of an explicitly named cap.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-NAVIGATE require fixed Grip frames in solving-workflow.md section 4.3. The twelve proper frames and their legal witnesses are model mathematics retained by charter section 2.
requirements: Return all twelve proper cap frames with exact corner order, model identity and finite legal frame witnesses.
Keep frame choice explicit and independent of camera, filters and changing occupants; no view change may silently alter a Twist key's meaning.
Retain access to all 1,200 generators even when ergonomic key sets or views show a subset.

rows.purpose: Discover and copy installed Managed DirectX assemblies into the retained native runtime cache.
rows.reason: This diagnostic serves only the retained MPUlt/Managed DirectX host, excluded by charter section 4 and section 5 anti-goal 1. F-PLATFORM checks for the selected 1.0 backend replace that obsolete dependency rather than preserving its cache preparation.
rows.notes: Removal concerns this Managed DirectX copying check, not general package integrity, platform capability diagnostics or preservation of upstream licence notices.

rows.purpose: Understand the exact forward and inverse corner actions of each local Twist axis.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-NAVIGATE retain the Grip/Twist grammar in solving-workflow.md section 4.3. Deriving corner cycles from actual vertex actions preserves the mathematical contract of charter section 2.
requirements: Derive H/T axis cycles, inverses, fixed corners and orders from the actual model vertex permutation, not a cosmetic drawing or current camera.
Use exact ordered frames and glossary-backed notation with static equivalents; shown facts must have the mathematical basis required by charter section 5 M1-M4.
Explanations of directions never choose a turn, construct a solving macro or change the puzzle.

rows.purpose: Produce an isolated distributable application package bound to verified sources, assets, tools and licences.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM and charter section 5 E7 retain traceable distribution, while charter section 4 replaces the 0.4 frozen launcher/engine and retained native payload. Assembly and its optional archive remain one packaging purpose, to be rebuilt for the selected 1.0 runtime after stage 2.
requirements: X-01: Verify the canonical checkout bytes and exact packaged model/proof bytes against their bound hashes before accepting assembly.
Require approved pinned tools, explicit source/model/proof inputs, an accepted build receipt and fresh output/work destinations; recheck inputs before publishing an accepted package.
Reject unexpected payloads, architecture mismatches, user data, credentials and personal logs; preserve existing outputs instead of overwriting them.
Preserve Andrey Astrelin's primary MPUlt credit and upstream licence notices and never redistribute Microsoft Managed DirectX DLLs.
Bind any optional archive and its digest to the same verified package; a packaging command does not install, upload, publish or claim release acceptance.
Keep release packaging out of stage 2 implementation and do not inherit the 0.4 PyInstaller layout or retained runtime dependencies.

rows.purpose: Translate a solver-chosen cap, proper Grip frame and Twist direction into an exactly equivalent legal move word.
rows.reason: F-COMPOSE and F-EXECUTE retain explicit Grip/Twist input under solving-workflow.md sections 4.1 and 4.3. This compiles the solver's chosen physical turn and its witness, not a program-chosen solving macro (charter sections 2 and 5).
requirements: Validate cap, proper ordered frame, axis and inverse flag and prove the emitted legal word equal on every one of the 259,800 labels.
Distinguish the emitted word from a conjugating proof witness; Strict protection checks the chronological word actually executed.
Keep all 1,200 generators reachable and key meanings fixed independently of camera, filtering and piece movement.
Resolution is detached; draft input only appends to the selected phase, while live input requires its own current protection check and explicit solver action.

rows.purpose: Verify an installed candidate's integrity, recovery and data round trips through explicit isolated acceptance diagnostics.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM retains acceptance evidence for the product, and F-MIGRATE retains one-way recovery guarantees under the 2 October 2026 migration decision. Charter section 4 requires new-runtime diagnostics instead of acceptance of the 0.4 frozen and Managed DirectX payload.
requirements: Use fresh synthetic sessions and verified fixture copies for package tampering, transaction/reopen, ownership, log/library/keymap and migration scenarios; never use personal data.
Bind every component report to its exact source/build/model and restore deliberately altered fixture artifacts even after failure.
Replace the frozen-launcher and Managed DirectX checks with the selected 1.0 platform contract, retaining integrity, licences, durable receipts and recovery proof.

A database migration fixture must use the session lock and SQLite online backup, leave the original unchanged and avoid immutable=1; actual importer work still requires Windows probes P1-P3 and the format-freeze gate.
Separate source/fixture, synthetic geometry, actual Windows/DirectX and performance evidence; headless acceptance cannot stand in for a native window, GPU, input, long session or release sign-off.

rows.purpose: Obtain the model-bound cut-cell geometry needed to show actual local sticker regions and their hosting cells.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-RELATE need truthful geometry, while charter section 2 preserves the immutable model. Re-hosting the verified 433-region mesh and 600 cell transforms preserves that mathematical geometry contract.
requirements: Validate all 433 base regions and 600 transforms against the immutable model and expose vertices, region centres and triangle ranges with model identity.
Use geometry only as renderer/view input; rendering, triangulation, scaling or visibility must not change mechanical labels, cuts, IDs or legal generators.
Keep the mathematical geometry data independent of Windows and the retained runtime; the new views and materials are designed separately.

rows.purpose: Measure the component costs of representative commands and inspections on isolated reproducible fixtures.
rows.reason: F-PLATFORM supports the response and startup budgets of charter section 5 E2-E3. Profiling survives as an explicit development tool, but the 0.4 paired-reply and native-map stages are replaced by the 1.0 engine, command and view-model boundaries.
requirements: Use fresh fixed full-model fixture sessions, explicit commands and accepted reference inputs; preserve source/build/model digests, tool versions and the production command with results.
Measure only stages actually executed and report sampling, payload sizes and context; do not infer physical-input, renderer, GPU or end-to-end latency from in-process component timings.
Separate correctness from time and bind before/after inputs to the measured candidate; never profile personal sessions by default.
Keep profiling out of normal startup and gate fixture turns through the same protection and command rules as ordinary operations.

rows.purpose: Inspect every committed sticker and physical occupant of a selected canonical cell with its frame and protection context.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-CHECK need exact Local observations in solving-workflow.md section 4. The 433-slot committed-state observation remains a contract even though the Global and Local presentation is redesigned under charter section 5 D8.
requirements: Return all 433 canonical slots with actual labels, physical identities, affecting caps, explicit proper frame, filter matches and protected positions from one snapshot.
Bind Current, Next, buffers, protection, full-state hash and revision to the same context used by both views.
Treat colour-cell IDs as exact model facts rather than identity inferred from rendered colour, and keep filters separate from full protection and effect analysis.
Do not substitute predicted labels for committed occupants or mutate state during cell inspection.
rows.notes: D-02 is recorded as rejected in units.json and screening-findings.md; this proposal does not revive that optimization lead as an open requirement.

rows.purpose: Maintain descriptive names, notes, tags and pinning for the solver's macros without changing their recipes.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-REUSE retain the solver's own macro base in solving-workflow.md sections 4 and 7. Validated metadata edits leave exact recipe and content identity unchanged.
requirements: Validate metadata and return an independent record while preserving normalized recipe, exact revision and content identity.
Persist changes through the command layer and session store, with workspace revisions and durable failure handling rather than a second mutation path.
Names, tags and imported descriptive claims must not certify effect, applicability, completion or permission.

rows.purpose: Find the solver's existing macros by descriptive metadata and verified complete-effect facts.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-REUSE need a macro base by orbit and use in solving-workflow.md section 6. Exact facets over existing records aid selection without choosing a macro for the solver, as section 7 requires.
requirements: Combine only explicit metadata and complete locally checked effect facts, retaining collateral orbits and separating unknown verification from an empty result.
Keep pinned, tags, affected orbits, effect kind and likely-use membership distinct; a use facet is not current applicability or execution permission.
Return catalogue records for the solver to select without inserting, generating or executing a solving macro.

rows.purpose: Export explicitly selected personal macros with exact recipes and provenance for archival or reuse.
rows.reason: F-REUSE retains saving and reusing the solver's own macros under solving-workflow.md sections 4 and 7. The exported document is redesigned for the 1.0 format and layer boundary rather than inheriting the 0.4 schema as authority.
requirements: Export only explicitly selected distinct exact revisions, normalized legal recipes, metadata, model identity and descriptive derivation, under documented resource limits.
Ensure the product can import its own export within the same limits; derived effects and applicability are recomputed locally, not trusted from the file.
Treat geometric derivation and imported certificates as claims until checked against the current model and frames.
Keep document construction detached; file writes go through the command layer to an explicit destination and never publish or upload data.
rows.notes: The format is a proposal for the appropriate 1.0 freeze; no schema is changed by this packet.

rows.purpose: Review an entire macro-library document and its conflicts before importing any entry.
rows.reason: F-REUSE and F-MACRO retain reuse of explicitly supplied macros under solving-workflow.md section 7. Charter section 4 and AGENTS.md transactional import rules put validation in the engine and the accepted batch in one session-store operation with a 1.0 document contract.
requirements: Validate the complete document, model, schema, resource limits and every normalized legal recipe before any database write.
Report added, identical and conflicting revisions; preserve local metadata for identical entries and never silently replace a conflicting recipe.
Bind confirmation to exact file digest and current workspace/model revisions and recompute effect and reference evidence locally.
Keep inspection detached; apply only the confirmed conflict-free batch transactionally through the command layer with current preferences and recovery intact.

rows.purpose: Classify a supplied macro's complete action by exact positional and orientation effects on every affected orbit.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-CHECK retain macro analysis under solving-workflow.md sections 2 and 4.1. Exact classification against an independent fixed chart preserves the mathematical contract of charter section 2.
requirements: Classify all affected orbits with complete support, cycle lengths and position/orientation counts, including collateral outside the target orbit.
A pure positional cycle requires every edge to agree with the independent fixed slot chart; unavailable chart evidence remains Unknown.
Keep body classification separate from complete Prepare/Macro/Cleanup permission and never use classification to choose or output a solving recipe.

rows.purpose: Recognize certified star relations already present in an explicitly supplied complete operation.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-CHECK retain analysis of the solver's own macros under solving-workflow.md section 7. Recognition keeps the retained-seed and full orbit-local equality guarantees of charter section 2 without constructing an insertion.
requirements: Report explicit A/B/target positions, ordered frames and the matching retained-seed certificate only when the complete orbit-local action is equal.
Retain all collateral effects and distinguish a scoped star relation from a globally pure operation.
Recognize supplied relations only; do not infer a target and emit a new star macro from the current state.

rows.purpose: Explain which orbit uses an existing macro appears suited to from its checked intrinsic effects.
rows.reason: F-MACRO retains explained organization by orbit and use in solving-workflow.md section 6. The 0.4 heuristic memberships are redesigned as versioned explanations under command-table.md section 1, separate from evidence and permission.
requirements: Score only locally checked complete effects of existing macros, disclosing rule version, contributions, thresholds, exclusions and unavailable evidence.
Intrinsic likely use is independent of the current target and protection; it does not certify current applicability, completion or execution safety.
Use memberships as catalogue facts for solver choice, never automatic macro selection, insertion or generation.

rows.purpose: Understand how an existing macro's body effects intersect the solver's current orbit and protected work.
rows.reason: F-MACRO and F-CHECK retain contextual analysis under solving-workflow.md sections 2 and 4.1. Explaining intersections preserves intrinsic macro facts while the complete operation is reviewed separately.
requirements: Report every affected orbit's relation to current, completed and protected work using the current protection revision.
Body-level damage or apparent safety must not substitute for the full Prepare/Macro/Cleanup protection check.
Context highlights do not change intrinsic memberships or select a solving macro, and unknown effect evidence stays explicit.

rows.purpose: Resolve a copied typed sticker-slot address to its exact canonical location.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-NAVIGATE retain exact object addressing, but the 2 October 2026 design decision section 2 gives 1.0 one mathematical language and encoding grammar. Its parser follows the agreed naming version while charter section 2 keeps model identity and canonical IDs unchanged.
requirements: Validate the entire Slot type, naming version, model identity, hosting-cell pole, structure class and region word before returning a canonical sticker slot.
Reject stale, unsupported, ambiguous or partially parsed addresses rather than guessing a piece or position.
Keep parsing independent of camera, filters and occupant changes; any supported legacy format must resolve to the same immutable slot.
Define the user-visible address grammar and relied-on facts in the glossary and theory book at the reduced scope of the 2 October 2026 scope decision.

rows.purpose: Resolve a copied typed fixed-position address independently of its current occupant.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-NAVIGATE retain exact destinations in solving-workflow.md section 4. The 2 October 2026 design decision section 2 redesigns the address language while preserving the distinction between position and occupant and the immutable model IDs.
requirements: Validate the complete Position type, naming version, model and geometric address before returning the canonical fixed physical position.
Never reinterpret the address as its occupant, a piece identity or an inferred destination frame, and reject ambiguous or unsupported versions.
Keep the resolved position stable under turns, filters and camera changes and compatible with any explicitly supported legacy address grammar.
Document and review the visible position/occupant distinction in the shared mathematical grammar; naming changes must not change model identity.

rows.purpose: Resolve a copied typed piece address to the immutable physical identity anchored at Home.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-REUSE require tracking identities as pieces move (solving-workflow.md sections 4 and 4.3). The 2 October 2026 design decision section 2 redesigns names and exact IDs together without changing the model boundary.
requirements: Validate the entire Piece type, declared naming version, model and immutable Home address before returning the canonical physical identity.
Reject unsupported or ambiguous addresses and never resolve a Piece address to the current occupant of its Home.
Identity remains unchanged across turns, filters and camera changes; any supported old grammar must name that same identity.
Define visible Piece/Home terms in the shared glossary and theory book without adding background mathematics outside the approved 1.0 scope.

rows.purpose: Identify a canonical cell and its exact supported geometric pole.
rows.reason: F-RELATE and F-LEARN retain truthful cell identification under charter section 5 M1-M4. The 2 October 2026 design and scope decisions require intuitive names from one glossary, with exact IDs and only the visible mathematics documented.
requirements: Keep C1-C600 canonical identities tied to the actual model geometry; naming or visual encoding must not relabel cells or pieces.
Show supported exact golden-coordinate values and coordinate order, and disclose reconstruction tolerance or approximation wherever used.
Use one agreed term, notation and exact ID per concept, defining and proving only facts needed by the visible encoding.

rows.purpose: Distinguish every orbit by its exact incidence, orientation structure and immutable identity.
rows.reason: F-TARGET, F-MACRO and F-LEARN need orbit-first context (solving-workflow.md sections 2 and 6). The 2 October 2026 design decision section 2 redesigns orbit names and diagrams while charter section 2 preserves the complete model census.
requirements: Retain canonical orbit IDs, exact hosting/cap incidences, sticker counts, orientation group and fixed centres; coarse counts or repeated colours cannot identify an orbit.
Keep captions and representative portraits unambiguous and tied to actual geometry within the shared glossary and visible encoding grammar.
Do not use ID order or a caption rank as the certified collateral-dependent solve order; name that order separately.

rows.purpose: Describe and copy an exact sticker-slot location with a typed model-bound address.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-NAVIGATE retain precise inspection and copyable object references. The 2 October 2026 design decision section 2 puts IDs, relations and naming in one picture-first grammar rather than carrying over the 0.4 caption format.
requirements: Produce unambiguous versioned Slot copy text that round-trips to the same immutable slot through its matching parser.
Distinguish canonical cell/region/frame data from approximate centroid hints; a geometric region word is not a setup instruction or orientation certificate.
Use the agreed glossary and address grammar with real-geometry explanations, respecting the owner's text budgets and reduced theory scope.

rows.purpose: Describe and copy a fixed physical position with its hosting cells and affecting caps.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-COMPOSE require fixed destinations and buffers in solving-workflow.md sections 3.1 and 4. The 2 October 2026 design decision section 2 redesigns exact language while retaining the position/occupant distinction.
requirements: Generate a versioned Position address without consulting the current occupant and make it round-trip to the same canonical position.
Return all exact hosting cells and affecting caps; ergonomic hosting choices must not truncate the legal affecting set.
Keep position, piece identity, buffer role and slot frame as separate typed facts in the agreed encoding and glossary.

rows.purpose: Relate an immutable piece Home to its current physical location using exact typed names.
rows.reason: F-FIND and F-RELATE retain the solver's need to compare Home with Current in solving-workflow.md section 4. The 2 October 2026 design decision sections 2 and 6 redesigns the language for linked Local and Global context without changing identity.
requirements: Check identity and location share the legal orbit and return immutable Home, current position and orbit/symmetry facts from one committed revision.
Produce typed Piece copy text distinct from Position and Slot addresses and ensure exact round trips under the declared naming version.
Keep geometric address words and approximate centroids distinct from legal setup witnesses and orientation evidence.
Use one shared context and glossary for both views; labels and colour classes must never substitute for physical identity or exact frame evidence.

rows.purpose: Verify the complete geometric correspondence between two explicitly chosen proper reference frames.
rows.reason: F-RELATE and F-REUSE retain checking the solver's own references under solving-workflow.md section 7. The correspondence is detached analysis, preserving charter section 2's prohibition on mechanical relabelling.
requirements: Check a unique proper full cell, sticker-slot and piece mapping preserving every legal orbit, bound to model, manifest and mapping hashes.
Keep source and destination frames explicit and independent of current Grip, camera and state.
A verified geometric correspondence is neither a puzzle move nor proof of execution safety; never relabel actual mechanical state.

rows.purpose: Inspect exact fixed-position and sticker-slot correspondences under a verified chosen geometric reference.
rows.reason: F-RELATE and F-REUSE retain reference inspection under solving-workflow.md sections 3.3 and 7. This detached correspondence preserves charter section 2's model and mechanical-label boundary.
requirements: Validate the explicit proper reference pair and distinct supplied positions, preserving the bounded request and every source/destination slot pair.
Bind results to model and mapping hashes and preserve legal orbit identities.
Keep mapping analytical only; it neither moves pieces nor establishes a target orientation or execution permission without the corresponding evidence.

rows.purpose: Reuse an explicitly selected existing macro in a solver-chosen geometric reference with a verified legal witness.
rows.reason: F-REUSE permits transforms and reuse of the solver's own macros under solving-workflow.md sections 4.1 and 7. Unlike endgame recipe generation, this compilation starts with an exact supplied macro revision and explicit frames, preserving charter section 2's full-effect witnesses.
requirements: Require the exact solver-selected source revision and explicit proper source/destination frames; never infer a solution or retarget from residuals.
Verify every transformed primitive and the complete chronological source-to-destination action on all 259,800 labels, retaining full collateral and provenance.
Return a finite emitted witness, exact cost and mapping/equality evidence under declared limits, with cancellation unable to publish a partial variant.
Compilation does not save, select or execute the result; any reuse requires a fresh complete-operation protection review of the emitted witness and current revisions.
Keep the analytical geometric relabelling separate from actual mechanical labels and immutable model identity.

rows.purpose: Read exact positional and orientation residuals for the current orbit and a bound predicted result.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and F-ENDGAME are driven by residuals under solving-workflow.md sections 3.4 and 6. Exact counts, buffer occupants and frame evidence remain mathematical contracts, not automatic choices of a target or correction macro.
requirements: Separate nonbuffer displacement, buffer occupancy, orientation-at-Home errors, unknown frames and raw exact-label status in one model-bound observation.
Distinguish Current from conditional After with base-state, recipe and revision identities and include complete Current-to-Home relations.
Keep necessary invariant evidence separate from reachability, protection and completion; missing evidence is explicit rather than a zero residual.
A work-intent-kind suggestion may describe the observed stage but must not choose a target, select a macro, emit a correction or execute an action.

rows.purpose: Determine whether every labelled position and orientation of an orbit is exactly complete.
rows.reason: F-ENDGAME and F-PROTECT require exact completion under solving-workflow.md section 3.4 and charter section 2. The Complete, Incomplete or Conditional evidence contract survives re-hosting.
requirements: Require exact Home labels for every slot in the orbit and a matching independent fixed frame with known operation scope.
Keep predicted After completion conditional until the corresponding committed Current state is verified; colours, empty graphs and missing candidates never certify completion.
Keep permitted nonidentity residuals and impossible residual diagnoses distinct from solved status.
Bind any completion receipt or protection transition to the exact model, orbit, state hash, frame and current operation evidence.

rows.purpose: Explain exact residual, buffer and protected-requirement changes between two supplied state endpoints.
rows.reason: F-EXECUTE and F-CHECK require before/after review in solving-workflow.md sections 4 and 4.1. Endpoint deltas remain exact observations of full collateral, with Net distinct from Strict protection.
requirements: Bind endpoints to the actual journal event or simulated operation and show residual counts, A/B occupants and labels, changed positions and captured-requirement gains/losses.
Include all affected labels and protected objects even outside the work or display filter, preserving captured states of protected unfinished orbits.
State that endpoint preservation is a Net observation and cannot prove every primitive prefix safe under Strict policy.
Keep legal execution, current progress and exact completion as separate facts and rederive actual deltas after commit or undo.

rows.purpose: Check a supplied orbit decomposition against certified necessary parity and orientation conditions.
rows.reason: F-ENDGAME retains diagnosis of impossible residuals in solving-workflow.md section 3.4. Matching all-generator certificate lookup and necessary-only conclusions preserve the mathematical and evidence contracts of charter sections 2 and 5 M3.
requirements: X-01: Load the pinned invariant proof and its declared source/model/frame hashes from canonical checkout and package bytes; line-ending conversion must not produce a false pass or silently stale evidence.
Check all 1,200 generators in the bound certificate and return Conflict, PassNecessary or Unavailable with exact parity and orientation quotient evidence.
Never promote a necessary-condition pass to reachability, protection or completion, and never compensate an impossible orbit residual in another orbit.
Certificate inspection must disclose missing, stale or mismatched proof without starting an unrequested audit or generating a correction macro.

rows.purpose: Obtain an immutable certified slot chart and finite orientation group for a named orbit position.
rows.reason: F-CHECK and F-ENDGAME require independent frame evidence in solving-workflow.md section 3.4. The complete transported-frame mathematics and legal witnesses remain binding under charter section 2.
requirements: Cover every position of the supplied orbit with exact ordered slots and finite orientation elements, checked against retained finite legal transports and model identity.
Keep the chart independent of current Grip, camera, filters and puzzle state and separate a geometric visual hint from certified orientation evidence.
Cache only complete immutable model/frame results; cancellation or failure cannot publish a partially built orbit certificate.
Expose unavailable or stale reference evidence explicitly rather than guessing orientation or granting permission.
rows.notes: The fixed transported slot chart is independent of the solver's selected cap Grip frame; a dependency on Grip-frame tooling does not make those purposes interchangeable. U6-033 is linked only for its finite orientation/reference inspection parts.

rows.purpose: Read the current attempt, elapsed time, journal statistics, source claims and bound completion receipts together.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-LEARN retain interruption-safe progress and local learning measures in solving-workflow.md section 4.2 and the 2 October 2026 design decision section 5. The report is redesigned across the six layers, preserving exact state and evidence while keeping timing outside mathematical decisions.
requirements: Bind attempt identity, journal head, full-state hash, exact whole-model Home status and completion receipts to one current snapshot.
Separate recorded source/assistance claims from locally verified evidence, and separate elapsed time and learning attainment from correctness and exact completion.
Keep timer and any in-situ metrics local in the session store; the mathematical engine must not read the clock for decisions and nothing is uploaded.
Present completion only from a receipt matching the current attempt and committed state; reset or imported Home labels alone do not count as an earned solve.
Use short reviewed language and noninterrupting progress content under the owner's design decisions, without requiring completion acknowledgement.

rows.purpose: Continue the existing attempt with its saved working context and current authoritative state.
rows.reason: F-SESSION retains interruption and resume in solving-workflow.md section 4.2. The 2 October 2026 design decision section 7 requires direct resume in one entry, so 1.0 restores shared context rather than merely returning the 0.4 report.
requirements: Retain attempt identity, drafts, roles, references, macro revisions, block and locked Next without resetting or replacing shared mechanical state.
Resolve each saved identity's current position again, invalidate execution permission and keep current global protection instead of restoring an old policy.
Resume must not implicitly start the timer, generate a macro or execute saved steps; all later execution needs a fresh review.
Update both linked views from one recovered context and revision and disclose missing or stale reference inputs.

rows.purpose: Explicitly start or pause the attempt timer while retaining elapsed thinking time.
rows.reason: F-SESSION retains an explicit timer and its statistics through interruptions. F-LEARN reports time separately from correctness under the 2 October 2026 design decision section 5; no automatic solving or timer-triggered action is introduced.
requirements: Keep start and pause explicit, preserve the attempt baseline and include thinking time in elapsed attempt duration.
Persist timer state through the command layer and session store without making elapsed time an engine decision or execution gate.
Returning a report or resuming an attempt must not reset the timer or implicitly start it; exports use the same attempt elapsed value.
Keep timing local and separate from correctness, assistance and completion evidence.
rows.notes: command-table.md section 5 leaves journal-versus-workspace ownership of session.timer.* open; this proposal preserves explicit timer semantics and does not settle its storage/undo contract.

rows.purpose: Prepare a reproducible legal random scramble with recorded seed and provenance for an explicitly chosen attempt.
rows.reason: F-LEARN and F-SESSION retain the full-model practice copy and recorded attempt setup in the 2 October 2026 design decision section 7. This is an explicitly requested scramble, not a solving macro or automatic execution under solving-workflow.md section 7.
requirements: C-04: Validate draft edits before changing pending scramble provenance; a rejected edit must preserve the seed, recipe hash, source classification and prior pending operation exactly.
Record the supplied or generated seed, normalized chronological legal primitives and recipe hash under the existing bounded scramble contract.
Keep recipe preparation detached and preserve any previous pending preview, including on failure or cancellation.
Stage or apply only on an explicit solver action with a fresh full-state and protection review; never reset or unlock a real solve automatically.
A practice copy uses all 259,800 labels and all 1,200 generators and is clearly separate from the solver's ongoing session.

rows.purpose: Save a verifiable attempt log with its exact witness history and elapsed time to an explicit local destination.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-REUSE retain saving work through interruption in solving-workflow.md section 4.2. Charter section 4 puts serialization and file writes behind the session-store and command boundaries, with a 1.0 format independent of the retained runtime.
requirements: Retain complete legal witnesses in chronological order, model identity, transaction/state evidence and the same attempt timer value used by reports.
Preserve the fixed A-02 guarantee: a saved log must pass the product's own import limits and validation; refuse an over-budget log before writing and offer a session archive.
Choose the destination explicitly and write recoverably without changing puzzle state, preferences or existing recovery data.
Use approved 1.0 serialization and explicitly supported compatibility conversions without requiring Managed DirectX or launching the 0.4 runtime.

rows.purpose: Obtain verifiable attempt-log bytes with elapsed time for an explicitly chosen archival destination.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-REUSE retain exporting the solver's work under solving-workflow.md section 4.2. The document contract and file boundary are redesigned for 1.0 while exact witness and timer semantics remain.
requirements: Construct a detached model-bound log from the exact journal branch, complete chronological witnesses and current attempt elapsed time.
Retain the fixed A-02 export/import round-trip guarantee and reject data above supported limits before returning an unusable log.
Keep byte generation separate from explicit file writing and from any upload or publication.
Label source claims and locally verified evidence separately; serialization changes remain subject to the appropriate format contract and freeze.

rows.purpose: Validate and privately replay an entire log before confirming a possible import.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-REUSE retain read-before-import safety under AGENTS.md Persistence and process ownership. Charter section 4 puts 1.0 format validation and mathematical replay behind one confirmation contract rather than trusting legacy runtime data.
requirements: Validate the entire format, model, transaction structure, redo tail, resource limits and legal witnesses and replay them on detached full-model state before writes.
Bind confirmation to exact file bytes/digest, format, current state/head, workspace/protection/preferences and any required mapping evidence.
Imported preferences, assistance claims and certificates are data, not authority; never adopt them as current policy or verified evidence.
Disclose unsupported legacy formats or unknown mappings explicitly; any supported conversion runs without personal data or the retained host.
Maintain export/import limit compatibility and leave the existing database, pending operation and recovery checkpoint unchanged during inspection.

rows.purpose: Import only freshly confirmed log bytes as one recoverable session operation.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-REUSE retain explicit import with preserved work under AGENTS.md transactional import rules. The 1.0 command and session-store boundaries in charter section 4 keep successful commit distinct from a failed display refresh.
requirements: Require an explicit solver action and the identical inspected bytes, format and still-current confirmation context; recheck full-state hash and workspace/protection revisions before commit.
Validate complete replay before writes, import atomically, keep current preferences and retain a recoverable checkpoint of the previous state.
Publish a durable command receipt and at-most-once outcome; a later status or snapshot failure reports applied with display stale rather than failed.
Cancel or reject without partial state changes, reconcile an unknown durable outcome before retry, and invalidate old previews and confirmations after application.
Keep the original 0.4 database migration separate: path B uses a locked SQLite backup, never modifies the source and remains subject to its unrun Windows prerequisites.

rows.purpose: Record exact whole-puzzle completion and attempt statistics when an explicit operation finishes the full model.
rows.reason: F-ENDGAME and F-LEARN require exact completion and earned progress in solving-workflow.md section 3.4 and the 2 October 2026 design decision section 1. A detached summary bound to the finishing operation is published only with its successful atomic commit.
requirements: Require transition from unfinished to all 259,800 exact Home labels, including required fixed structures, with matching evidence for every moving orbit's independent frame.
Bind the summary to attempt identity, exact pending recipe and pre/post state hashes and publish it in the same durable commit receipt.
Predicted completion remains conditional; reset, imported Home labels, missing certificates or colour matches alone cannot create an earned completion receipt.
Keep timer, move statistics and recorded assistance distinct from mathematical completion and give them the same attempt context.
Undo withdraws the current achievement and pending celebration while keeping unlocked explanations and saved macros; any whole-puzzle moment is quiet and in place.

rows.purpose: Remember that the current verified completion summary has been seen without requiring a separate acknowledgement action.
rows.reason: F-LEARN and F-SESSION retain seen-summary bookkeeping, but the 2 October 2026 design decision section 1 requires small in-place rewards that never interrupt input. Automate only this receipt bookkeeping, within solving-workflow.md section 7's boundary.
requirements: Mark seen only when the exact matching current completion receipt is actually presented; bind it to attempt identity, receipt identity and committed state hash.
Reject stale receipts and never infer completion from presentation or acknowledgement, a score or a timer.
Store bookkeeping locally through the command/session boundary with no modal acknowledgement, macro choice, generated solution or automatic execution.
Undo immediately withdraws the current achievement and pending celebration while retaining explanations already unlocked and macros already saved; preserve access to the recorded summary.
rows.notes: Proposed automate disposition requires owner sign-off after integration; this packet neither authorizes nor implements the behavioural change.

rows.purpose: Capture the solver's fixed Prepare/Macro/Cleanup method with exact roles, reference and macro revisions for later reuse.
rows.reason: F-REUSE retains work sheets under solving-workflow.md sections 4 and 4.1. Capturing the solver's own fixed operation and comparison inputs is allowed by section 7 and does not choose or execute a solving macro.
requirements: Capture model identity, exact ordered phase steps, source macro revisions, reference word, goal, orbit, Current/destination, A/B, block, frame requirement and protection inputs.
Return an independent sheet without mutating state or the library; saving goes through the command/session boundary.
Keep fixed recipes and original bindings rather than a generated solver policy, and treat saved protection inputs as comparison context rather than authority.
Every later use needs current binding comparison and a fresh whole-operation protection review.

rows.purpose: Compare a saved fixed work sheet with the solver's live bindings and macro revisions before reuse.
rows.reason: F-REUSE retains explicit comparison in solving-workflow.md section 4.1, where reuse never reuses a review. The same, missing, changed and unknown comparison semantics carry into 1.0 without silent retargeting.
requirements: Validate the sheet and report saved/live role, target, buffer, block, reference, frame and protection differences plus exact source-revision match, changed or missing status.
Retain fixed steps unchanged, and keep legacy fixed sheets inspectable with missing provenance or policy explicitly unknown.
A role or target mismatch and a protection conflict must be visible; comparison alone never certifies applicability or grants execution permission.
Re-normalize legal recipes and review the complete emitted witness against current full state and protection before any explicit execution.

rows.purpose: Evaluate the exact goal the solver chose against supplied before and after states.
rows.reason: F-CHECK retains goal analysis under solving-workflow.md sections 3.3 and 4.1. Met, Unmet, Unknown, MissingInput and NotApplicable remain separate from legality and permission, including legal preparation that does not yet improve the goal.
requirements: Use explicit prepare, insert, place, orient, finish-buffer, block or endgame bindings without choosing or changing the solver's goal.
Distinguish position-only placement from exact identity/orientation labels and require matching paired-frame evidence for orientation and endgame claims.
Label all predicted After results conditional and expose missing input or unknown evidence instead of falsely reporting a failed goal.
Keep goal achievement separate from the complete-operation legality/protection gate and exact orbit or whole-puzzle completion.

rows.purpose: Save and recall per-orbit working choices while retaining the current global protection policy.
rows.reason: F-SESSION and F-TARGET retain orbit return and interruption semantics in solving-workflow.md section 4.2. Detached context switching and the fixed C-02 atomic persistence guarantee remain contracts at the 1.0 session boundary.
requirements: Save departing context and restore exact Current, destination, buffers, draft steps/sources, block, selected macro, reference and Local centre, or explicit new-orbit defaults.
Keep global protection current; an old context must not roll back locks or silently reinterpret saved identities.
Resolve current piece locations again and invalidate execution permission on return or switch; both linked views receive one context and revision.
Retain the fixed C-02 guarantee by persisting active session orbit and workspace/context in one transaction; any save failure leaves both unchanged.

rows.purpose: See explained unfinished members and nearby extensions of the solver's current block as target candidates.
rows.reason: F-TARGET retains explained candidates under solving-workflow.md section 3.3. Redesign the 0.4 automatic-candidate flag into solver-confirmed suggestions with existing-macro and protection evidence, as required by sections 4 and 7.
requirements: List unsatisfied explicit block members in saved order and extend an exact Home block only through actual shared hosting-cell incidence on the active orbit.
State why each target continues the current context and fits the block boundary, whether a solver-owned existing macro matches, and whether current protection can remain unchanged.
Distinguish buffer A/B work from ordinary candidates and disclose unknown applicability rather than inventing a reference for a non-Home block.
Do not change the active target, choose or output a solving macro or execute an operation merely because a candidate is first; leave activation to the solver and honour locked Next priority.
An exhausted candidate list with residuals remaining leads to endgame inspection, never to a completion claim or automatic unlock.
rows.notes: No distinct cross-shard unit with the same block-candidate generation purpose is identified. Pinning or activating Next is a separate solver action, not evidence that its controls generate these candidates.

rows.purpose: Continue after an explicitly committed operation with preserved context, explained next work and verified completion protection.
rows.reason: F-TARGET and F-PROTECT retain continuation in solving-workflow.md sections 2, 3.3 and 4.2. Redesign implicit block-candidate promotion as an explained solver choice while preserving locked Next priority and transition-based protection.
requirements: Build a detached plan from exact bound before/after states and complete operation evidence; recheck preview, full-state hash and protection/workspace revisions before committing it.
Persist operation, context transition and eligible protection changes atomically with the durable command receipt; no partial continuation survives a failed commit.

For a successful checked insertion, honour the solver's previously locked Next, saving departing orbit context before a cross-orbit transition; show other candidates with reasons and require explicit activation.
Offer later-orbit inspection suggestions in the certified collateral-dependent order and wait for the solver; never choose a macro, execute another operation or force a stage.

Automatically add orbit protection only on a verified committed unfinished-to-exactly-solved transition; new/reset sessions are not blanket locked and an unchanged manually unlocked orbit stays unlocked.
Require a matching committed Current completion certificate after conditional planning, and distinguish protected, completed and selected objects.
Undo, redo, restore, reset and new-attempt paths rederive current residuals and invalidate reviews without masquerading as successful work-sheet insertion promotion.
rows.notes: Completion-transition protection is already automatic in the recorded workflow; this redesign does not introduce automatic solving. Goal progress, continuation choices and exact completion remain separate facts.
